ei.title: 코펜하겐 시의 자전거 이용 증진 정책
ei.subject: ReadingPower유형편완성

fullPassage: The City of Copenhagen has been restructuring its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a deliberate process to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it considerably safer to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is to increase this percentage considerably in the years to come.

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen has been ①<u>restructuring</u> its street network for several decades, ②<u>removing</u> driving lanes and parking places in a deliberate process to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, ③<u>separating</u> by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it considerably safer to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are ④<u>reflected</u> clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is to increase this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ separating → separated: bike paths가 curbs에 의해 분리된 것이므로 수동의 과거분사 separated가 필요. separating은 능동 현재분사로 의미 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ① restructuring: 원문 일치 (has been restructuring — 현재완료진행, 현재분사 OK)
✅ ② removing: 원문 일치 (removing ~ — 분사구문, 능동·동시동작 OK)
❌ ③ separating → separated (bike paths가 curbs에 의해 '분리되어 있는' 수동 관계 → 과거분사 separated 필수)
✅ ④ reflected: 원문 일치 (are reflected — 수동태, 과거분사 OK)
det.tip: 명사 수식 분사: 명사와 수동 관계 → 과거분사 / 능동·진행 관계 → 현재분사. bike paths는 curbs에 의해 '분리되므로' separated.

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen has been restructuring its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a deliberate process to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city ①<u>have been invited</u> to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings ②<u>painted in blue</u> and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, ③<u>make it considerably safer</u> to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work ④<u>were by bicycle</u>. The goal is to increase this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ were → was: 주어는 '37% of personal transport'로, percent + of + 불가산명사(transport) 구조에서 동사는 단수 was. were는 복수 수일치 오류.
det.analysis:
✅ ① have been invited: 원문 일치 (주어 the inhabitants 복수 + 현재완료 수동)
✅ ② painted in blue: 원문 일치 (bicycle crossings를 수식하는 수동 분사)
✅ ③ make it considerably safer: 원문 일치 (make + 가목적어 it + 형용사 safer — 진목적어 to cycle)
❌ ④ were → was (37% of personal transport — transport은 불가산, 비율 주어 단수 취급)
det.tip: percent + of + 명사: 뒤 명사가 불가산/단수 → 단수 동사. 37% of transport was (O) / were (X).

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen ①<u>has been restructuring</u> its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a deliberate process ②<u>to create</u> better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles ③<u>which turns green</u> six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it considerably safer to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is ④<u>to increase</u> this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ which turns → that turn: 선행사 special traffic lights for bicycles는 복수이므로 관계사절 동사는 turn(복수). turns는 단수 수일치 오류. 또한 콤마 없는 한정적 용법에는 that이 자연스럽고 복수이므로 turn이 필수.
det.analysis:
✅ ① has been restructuring: 원문 일치 (주어 The City — 단수 + 현재완료진행)
✅ ② to create: 원문 일치 (to부정사 목적 — 더 나은 환경을 만들기 위해)
❌ ③ which turns → that turn (선행사 special traffic lights = 복수. 관계사절 동사 turn 필수. turns는 단수 오류)
✅ ④ to increase: 원문 일치 (to부정사 주어 보어 — The goal is to increase)
det.tip: 관계대명사절 동사 수일치: 선행사가 복수이면 관계사절 동사도 복수. traffic lights (복수) → that turn (O) / turns (X).

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen has been restructuring its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a ①<u>deliberate</u> process to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an ②<u>effective</u> system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it considerably ③<u>harder</u> to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic ④<u>doubled</u> in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is to increase this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ harder(더 어려운) → safer(더 안전한): 자전거 신호등과 파란 횡단보도는 자전거 이용을 '더 안전하게' 만들기 위한 조치. harder(더 어렵게)는 글의 '자전거 친화 정책' 논지와 정반대.
det.analysis:
✅ ① deliberate: 원문 일치 (의도적인/계획된 — 코펜하겐의 '의도적' 정책 강조)
✅ ② effective: 원문 일치 (효과적인 — 자전거 도로 시스템을 효과적이라고 묘사)
❌ ③ harder → safer (자전거 신호 6초 먼저 + 파란 횡단보도 = '더 안전하게' 만드는 조치. harder는 반대 의미)
✅ ④ doubled: 원문 일치 (두 배로 증가 — 1995~2005 자전거 이용 두 배 증가)
det.tip: 앞 내용(신호등/파란 횡단보도) → 목적: 자전거 이용을 '더 안전하게'. safer와 대비해 harder는 논지 전도.

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen has been ①<u>restructuring</u> its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a deliberate process to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it considerably safer to cycle around the city. In short, a ②<u>half-hearted</u> invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are ③<u>reflected</u> clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is to ④<u>increase</u> this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② half-hearted(마지못한/미온적인) → whole-hearted(진심 어린): 앞 문장들에서 자전거 도로 시스템, 파란 횡단보도, 전용 신호등을 '의도적으로' 정비해 온 결과를 요약하는 위치. '진심 어린 초대'가 어울리고, half-hearted(미온적)는 이 맥락을 완전히 뒤집음.
det.analysis:
✅ ① restructuring: 원문 일치 (재구조화 — 도시 도로망을 수십 년간 재정비)
❌ ② half-hearted → whole-hearted (S1~S4의 적극적 정책 = '온 마음을 다한 초대'. half-hearted는 '미온적'으로 정반대 함의)
✅ ③ reflected: 원문 일치 (반영된 — 이용 패턴에 결과가 명확히 반영)
✅ ④ increase: 원문 일치 (높이다/증가시키다 — 비율을 더 늘리는 것이 목표)
det.tip: whole-hearted = 진심 어린, 전심으로 하는 ↔ half-hearted = 마지못한, 미온적인. 수십 년간의 정책 맥락상 whole-hearted가 필수.

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen has been restructuring its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a __________ to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it considerably safer to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is to increase this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: deliberate process(의도적인 과정): 코펜하겐이 수십 년에 걸쳐 차선과 주차 공간을 제거하며 자전거 환경을 만들어온 것은 '의도적이고 계획된 과정'이다. 즉흥적 결정이나 자연재해, 무작위 실험은 맥락과 어긋남.
det.analysis:
✅ ① deliberate process: '의도적인 과정' — 수십 년간의 계획적 재구조화(restructuring for several decades)와 완벽 호응
❌ ② sudden decision: '갑작스러운 결정' — decades에 걸친 점진적 과정과 모순
❌ ③ natural disaster: '자연재해' — 도시 정책과 무관
❌ ④ random experiment: '무작위 실험' — deliberate(계획적)의 반의어로 맥락 부정
det.tip: in a deliberate process = 의도적인 과정 속에서. removing lanes/parking = 수십 년 계획 실행 → deliberate.

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen has been restructuring its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a deliberate process to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it __________ to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is to increase this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: considerably safer(훨씬 더 안전한): 파란 자전거 횡단보도와 자전거 신호등이 차보다 6초 먼저 초록불이 켜지는 것은 자전거 이용을 '훨씬 더 안전하게' 만들기 위한 장치. 더 길거나, 비싸거나, 어렵게 만드는 것이 목적이 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ① considerably safer: '훨씬 더 안전한' — 파란 횡단보도 + 6초 선행 신호 모두 '안전' 목적과 직결
❌ ② slightly longer: '조금 더 긴' — 거리/시간 늘리기는 이 정책의 목적이 아님
❌ ③ far more expensive: '훨씬 더 비싼' — 자전거 이용 비용 언급 없음
❌ ④ increasingly difficult: '점점 더 어려운' — 글 전체 논지(자전거 친화)와 정반대
det.tip: make it + 형용사: 두 인프라 조치(파란 횡단보도 + 6초 선행 신호) → 목적 = safer. considerably = 상당히.

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen has been restructuring its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a deliberate process to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it considerably safer to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is to increase this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 자전거 신호등은 자동차보다 6초 먼저 초록불이 켜진다. 10초는 본문과 다른 수치.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 수십 년간 재구조화: S1 'for several decades' 일치
✅ ② 인도·차선과 분리된 자전거 도로: S3 'separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes' 일치
❌ ③ 10초 먼저 → 6초 먼저: S4 'six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward' — 10초 아니라 6초
✅ ④ 1995~2005 두 배 증가: S6 'Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005' 일치
det.tip: 수치 문항: six seconds. '10초'는 수치 교체 오답 패턴. 원문 숫자 6을 정확히 기억.

ch: 코펜하겐은 수십 년에 걸쳐 도로 네트워크를 재구조화해 왔다.
도시 전체에 인도 및 차선과 분리된 자전거 도로 시스템이 갖춰져 있다.
자전거용 신호등은 자동차보다 10초 먼저 초록불이 켜진다.
1995년부터 2005년 사이에 자전거 이용량이 두 배로 늘었다.

questions.passage: The City of Copenhagen has been restructuring its street network for several decades, removing driving lanes and parking places in a deliberate process to create better conditions for bicycle traffic. Year by year the inhabitants of the city have been invited to bike more. The entire city is now served by an effective system of bike paths, separated by curbs from sidewalks and driving lanes. City intersections have bicycle crossings painted in blue and, together with special traffic lights for bicycles that turn green six seconds before cars are allowed to move forward, make it considerably safer to cycle around the city. In short, a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists, and the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use. Bicycle traffic doubled in the period from 1995 to 2005, and in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle. The goal is to increase this percentage considerably in the years to come.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ② S6 'in 2008 statistics showed that 37% of personal transport to and from work was by bicycle' — 출퇴근 자전거 비율 37% 직접 일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 주민 자율에 맡김: S1 'in a deliberate process' — 시(city)가 의도적으로 주도 / 자율 방임 아님
✅ ② 2008년 출퇴근 자전거 37%: S6 문자적 일치
❌ ③ 빨간색: S4 'painted in blue' — 파란색
❌ ④ 인도와 합쳐져 있음: S3 'separated by curbs from sidewalks' — 인도와 분리
det.tip: 37% + to and from work + 2008년 — 세 가지 세부 정보 동시 일치 확인.

ch: 코펜하겐 시는 자전거 이용 환경 개선을 주민 자율에 맡겼다.
2008년 통계에 따르면 출퇴근 수단 중 자전거 비율이 37%였다.
코펜하겐의 자전거 도로는 인도와 합쳐져 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 'for several decades'(수십 년간) — 최근 5년 이내 시작이 아니라 수십 년 전부터 지속해 온 정책.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 이용 패턴에 명확히 반영: S5 'the results are reflected clearly in patterns of use' 일치
✅ ② 비율 더 늘리는 것이 목표: S7 'The goal is to increase this percentage considerably' 일치
✅ ③ 파란색 자전거 횡단보도: S4 'bicycle crossings painted in blue' 일치
❌ ④ 최근 5년 이내 시작: S1 'for several decades' — 수십 년간 지속. 5년 이내는 사실 왜곡
det.tip: several decades = 수십 년 (보통 20~30년+). '최근 5년'은 수십 년을 수년으로 축소한 오답.

ch: 자전거 이용 증가 결과는 이용 패턴에 명확히 반영되었다.
코펜하겐 시는 자전거 이용 비율을 앞으로 더 늘리는 것을 목표로 한다.
도시 교차로에는 파란색 자전거 횡단보도가 설치되어 있다.
코펜하겐은 자전거 친화 정책을 최근 5년 이내에 처음 시작하였다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주제: 코펜하겐이 수십 년간 의도적으로 자전거 도로·신호 인프라를 정비하고, 그 결과 자전거 이용이 두 배로 늘어 37%에 달하는 성과를 거뒀다는 내용.

det.tip: 키워드: restructuring + bicycle infrastructure + doubled + 37% = 정책 + 성과. ②③④ 모두 본문 범위 초과.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 제목: '수십 년간의 노력으로 자전거를 생활화시킨 코펜하겐' — S1 'for several decades'의 장기 정책 + S6 37% 출퇴근 이용률로 자전거가 생활방식이 된 성과를 압축.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 수십 년간 노력 + 자전거 생활화: S1 'for several decades' + S6 37% 이용률 = 제목 정확 압축
❌ ② 자전거 도로 경제적 비용: 본문에 비용 언급 전혀 없음
❌ ③ 보행자-자전거 갈등: 본문은 분리(separated)로 갈등 방지, 갈등 논의 없음
❌ ④ 북유럽 대중교통 통계: 대중교통 통계 글 아님 — 자전거 특화 정책 글
det.tip: 제목 핵심 = 기간(수십 년) + 주체(코펜하겐) + 결과(자전거 생활화). S1+S6이 제목 두 축.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'a whole-hearted invitation has been given to cyclists'는 문자적으로 '자전거 이용자들에게 진심 어린 초대가 주어졌다'는 뜻. 앞 S1~S4에서 도로 재구조화, 자전거 도로, 파란 횡단보도, 전용 신호등이라는 구체적 인프라 정비가 바로 그 '초대'의 내용. 즉 시 당국이 수십 년간 전심으로 자전거 환경을 만들어 온 것을 함축.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 공식 초대장 우편 발송: 'invitation'을 문자 그대로 오해한 오답. 인프라 정책을 가리키는 비유적 표현
✅ ② 오랜 기간 자전거 환경 조성: S1~S4의 deliberate restructuring + bike paths + blue crossings + 6-sec lights = whole-hearted invitation의 내용
❌ ③ 연간 행사 개최: 본문에 행사 언급 없음
❌ ④ 자전거 이용자 자발 참여 요청: 주체가 시(city), 이용자에게 '초대'한 것. 이용자의 자발적 참여 요청과는 다름
det.tip: whole-hearted invitation = 진심 어린 초대 (비유). 앞 S1~S4 인프라 조치 전체가 이 '초대'의 구체적 내용. In short(요약)가 단서.
